name: No-Bake Maple Oat Energy Balls
description: Soft, poppable energy balls that travel well in a vest pocket. Fast-digesting carbs from oats and maple with just enough fat and protein to hold together.
instructions: In a bowl, stir together the rolled oats, nut butter, maple syrup and a pinch of salt until a sticky dough forms. Fold in the mini chocolate chips. Chill the mixture for 15 minutes so it firms up, then roll into 12 walnut-sized balls. Store in the fridge for up to a week, or pack into a zip bag for race day.
ingredients: 1/2 cup natural peanut or almond butter

name: Date and Almond Energy Bars
description: A homemade answer to shop-bought fruit-and-nut bars: dense, chewy, naturally sweet and entirely real-food. Cut into squares and wrap individually for the trail.
instructions: Pit the dates and soak in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain. Blitz the dates and almonds in a food processor until a sticky paste forms. Pulse in the oats, cocoa and a pinch of salt. Press the mixture firmly into a parchment-lined loaf tin, chill for 30 minutes, then cut into 10 bars. Wrap each in foil or parchment.

name: Nut Butter Rice Cakes
description: The portable savory-sweet rice cake long popular in pro cycling. Soft, easy on the stomach during long efforts, and quick to assemble the night before.
instructions: Cook the sushi rice with the water until soft and sticky. While still warm, stir through the nut butter, honey and a pinch of salt until evenly coated. Press firmly into a parchment-lined tray to about 2cm thick and chill for an hour. Cut into squares and wrap each one in foil so they stay easy to open mid-run.

name: Salted Sweet Potato Bites
description: Whole-food carbohydrate that sits gently in the gut when sweet gels stop working. Roasted soft, salted generously, and easy to pop one at a time.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200C. Peel and dice the sweet potato into 2cm cubes. Toss with the olive oil and a generous pinch of sea salt. Roast for 25-30 minutes until soft and caramelised at the edges, turning once. Cool completely, then pack into a zip bag. They keep for two days in the fridge.

name: Honey Nut Butter Tortilla Roll
description: Sixty seconds to make, endlessly stomachable: a soft tortilla wrapped around nut butter and honey. The ultra-runner's reliable real-food fallback.
instructions: Lay the tortilla flat and spread the nut butter edge to edge. Drizzle over the honey and sprinkle with a small pinch of salt. Roll up tightly, then wrap in foil and twist the ends. Slice into two if you want smaller portions on the move.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Sushi
description: A whole banana coated in peanut butter and oats, sliced into rounds. Sweet, soft and ready in minutes for the start line or a mid-run boost.
instructions: Peel the banana and coat it all over in a thin layer of peanut butter. Roll the coated banana in the rolled oats until covered. Slice into 2cm rounds. Pack flat in a small container so they don't squash. Best eaten within a few hours.

name: DIY Trail Mix
description: Build-your-own gorp with a deliberate balance of fast carbs, salt and slow-burning fat. Mix a big batch and portion into snack bags for every long run.
instructions: Combine the raisins, salted peanuts, pretzels and chocolate chips in a large bowl. Add a small pinch of extra salt if your peanuts are unsalted. Toss well, then divide into six small zip bags of roughly a handful each. Store in a cool, dry place.

name: Salted Boiled Potatoes
description: The classic ultra aid-station food. Plain boiled baby potatoes rolled in salt deliver carbohydrate and sodium with almost no chance of stomach upset.
instructions: Scrub the baby potatoes and boil in well-salted water for 12-15 minutes until just tender. Drain and let them steam-dry. While still warm, toss with the olive oil and roll in the flaky sea salt. Cool, then pack into a container or bag. They keep a day at room temperature.

name: Homemade Electrolyte Drink
description: A make-it-yourself sports drink with real carbohydrate and sodium, dialled to your taste instead of a fixed shop formula. Mix into a bottle before you head out.
instructions: In a 750ml bottle, combine the water, fruit juice, sugar or honey and salt. Add a squeeze of fresh citrus for flavour. Seal and shake hard until everything dissolves. Aim for roughly 30-60g of carbohydrate and a clear pinch of salt per bottle, and adjust strength to taste on long runs.
ingredients: Squeeze of fresh lemon or lime

name: Pumpkin Seed Cranberry Oat Bars
description: A lightly baked flapjack-style bar with chewy cranberries and crunchy pumpkin seeds. Sturdy enough to survive a hydration vest without crumbling.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180C and line a square tin. Gently melt the butter and honey together in a pan, then stir in the oats, pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries and a pinch of salt until evenly coated. Press firmly into the tin and bake for 20-22 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool fully in the tin before cutting into 9 bars.

name: Peanut-Stuffed Dates
description: No-cook fuel that goes straight from the packet into a vest pocket: sweet dates split and filled with salted peanut butter. Carb-dense, soft and effortless to chew mid-effort.
instructions: Slice each date lengthwise and pull out the stone. Spoon a little peanut butter into the opening, pinch the date closed and press a few flakes of sea salt on top. They travel best packed snugly in a small tub or wrapped in pairs so the filling stays put.

name: Banana and Oat Trail Cookies
description: Two-ingredient cookies that are almost all carbohydrate and hold together on the move. Naturally sweet from ripe bananas, no added sugar, and soft enough to eat while climbing.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180C and line a tray. Mash the bananas in a bowl, stir in the oats, cinnamon and a pinch of salt until the mixture is thick and evenly combined. Spoon into 10 small mounds on the tray, flatten slightly with the back of a spoon and bake for 15 minutes until set and lightly golden. Cool before stacking.

name: Puffed Rice and Honey Bars
description: Light, airy rice bars that are nearly pure fast carbohydrate. Cheaper than shop energy bars and easy to eat when your appetite is flagging late in a race.
instructions: Warm the honey and peanut butter in a pan over low heat until runny, then take off the heat. Stir in the puffed rice and a pinch of salt until every grain is coated. Press the mixture firmly into a lined loaf tin and chill for an hour until set, then cut into 8 bars. Keep them cool and they will not fall apart in a pocket.

name: Coconut Sticky Rice Bites
description: Chewy parcels of glutinous rice sweetened with coconut milk and maple. A gentle, easily digested carb hit that suits a tired stomach on long climbs.
instructions: Soak the sticky rice for at least an hour, then steam or simmer until tender. Warm the coconut milk with the maple syrup and salt and stir it through the cooked rice. Leave to absorb for 10 minutes, then shape into 8 small balls with damp hands and roll in toasted coconut. Wrap each one in a little cling film so they stay moist in the vest.

name: Rice Pudding Pouch
description: Comforting, spoonable carbs in a squeeze pouch for the point in a race when chewing is too much effort. Real food with almost no fibre to slow it down.
instructions: Simmer the cooked rice with the milk, honey, cinnamon and a pinch of salt for 8-10 minutes, stirring until thick and creamy. Blend briefly if you want it completely smooth, then cool and spoon into reusable pouches or a soft flask. Chill until needed and eat straight from the pouch on the move.

name: Miso Rice Balls
description: Savoury onigiri-style rice balls for when sweet fuel stops going down. Salty, plain carbs that are easy to eat with cold hands and taste like real food at hour five.
instructions: While the rice is still warm, stir the miso through it with a pinch of salt. With damp hands, press the rice into 6 compact triangles or balls, tucking a few sesame seeds into the middle of each. Wrap each one in cling film and keep them cool until you set off. Reach for these when you cannot face another sweet bite.

name: Mashed Potato Salt Flask
description: Ultra-running staple: soft, salty potato you can squeeze straight from a flask. No chewing, no crumbs and carbs that sit calmly on a churning stomach.
instructions: Boil the potatoes until completely soft, then mash with the olive oil, salt and enough warm water to make a smooth, spoonable paste. Push it through a sieve for a truly lump-free texture, then spoon into a reusable pouch or soft flask while still warm. Sip slowly and steadily rather than taking big mouthfuls.

name: Maple Lemon Carb Drink
description: A homemade carbohydrate bottle built for 60g-plus per hour when solid food is too much. Natural sugar, a pinch of salt and nothing you cannot pronounce.
instructions: In a 500ml bottle, dissolve the maple syrup and salt in the water, then add the lemon juice for flavour. Shake well before each sip so the sugar stays mixed. Sip steadily through the hour alongside solid food, and test the concentration on training runs before race day.
